_meta: AF/G.23 round, 2026-08-13. Djibouti municipal/régional-tier follow-up. Resolves af-djibouti.json's standing 'dj-loi-174-territorial' no-document dropped note: the national décentralisation law was independently located and primary-text-verified via two cross-confirming legal-text mirrors (droit-afrique.com and FAO's FAOLEX database), matching the branch's established precedent for mirror-hosted primary legal text (cf. dj-constitution-1992's MJP Digithèque hosting). Adds Djibouti-Ville's own organic statute (Loi 122/AN/05, fetched directly from the ministry's own .gouv.dj domain), the national organic finance law (Loi 107/AN/00), and four of five 2021-2025 Plans de Développement Régional (PDR) — government-authored planning/budget documents naming individual régions with real FDJ figures, exactly the 'higher tier of government reporting on named lower-tier units with figures' pattern this branch prioritizes. The fifth PDR (Arta) and a 2011 amendment law (Loi 149/AN/11) were located but only as AI-paraphrased fetch-tool summaries, not verbatim text, and are deferred rather than minted — see _dropped. Two web-portal sources (egouv.dj régions page, presidence.dj régions page) reported disagreeing population figures for the same régions/year; not resolved this round, logged as a note. Companion edit to af-djibouti.json updates dj-instad-cpi with a new technical confirmation of instad.dj's site-wide inaccessibility.

reports.title: Loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L du 7 juillet 2002 portant décentralisation et statut des régions
reports.description: Djibouti's national décentralisation law, creating the country's five régional collectivités territoriales. Article 2, verbatim: "Il est crée en République de Djibouti cinq collectivités territoriales régionales dénommées : Régions d'Arta, d'Ali Sabieh, de Dikhil, d'Obock et de Tadjourah...". Article 80, verbatim (on régional budget composition): "Le budget de la région est composé : Des dotations et transferts de État / Des ressources fiscales / Des produits de l'exploitation des services et domaines..." [the article "l'" before "État" is missing in this extraction — likely a PDF-extraction artifact of the mirror copy rather than a genuine textual variant; flagged for a cleaner-OCR re-check]. Article 93, verbatim: "Une dotation globale sera consentie par État pour assurer le fonctionnement des régions décentralisées" — the textual basis for the state-to-région fiscal-transfer mechanism (literal future-tense "sera consentie" in the original French; treated as prescriptive/statutory language per corpus convention). Article 4, verbatim: "Les Districts et Région d'Arta, dans leurs limites territoriales, ne comprennent pas Djibouti-Ville qui fera l'objet d'un statut spécial..." — the textual link establishing that Djibouti-Ville is carved out of the régional system and separately governed by its own statute (later enacted as Loi n°122/AN/05, see dj-loi-122-2005-ville-statut). Corroborated by Djibouti's own e-government portal (egouv.dj), which independently paraphrases the same law and states in its own text: "La région est dotée de la personnalité morale et de l'autonomie financière" [source rendering showed an encoding artifact in place of the apostrophes; corrected here] — though that portal's régional population figures for the same nominal 2021 reference year disagree with figures on presidence.dj (see _dropped note below, not resolved this round).

reports.title: Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L du 1er novembre 2005 portant statut de la Ville de Djibouti
reports.description: Djibouti-Ville's own organic statute law, fetched directly from the Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation's own .gouv.dj domain. Article 2, verbatim (defining the city's three communes): "La ville de Djibouti comprend trois communes : - la commune dénommée «Ras-Dika» dont le territoire correspond à celui du 6ème Arrondissement, - la commune appelée «Boulaos» recouvre l'ensemble des territoires de premier, deuxième et troisième arrondissement, - et la commune dite «Balbala» sous le nom duquel se regroupent les territoires du 4ème et du 5ème arrondissement." Article 99, verbatim (on the Conseil de Djibouti's budget composition): "Le budget du Conseil de Djibouti est composé : - des donations et transferts de l'État ; - des ressources fiscales locales ; - des produits de l'exploitation des services et domaines ; - des taxes rémunératrices sur les services rendus ; - des participations des autres collectivités ; - des produits financiers ; - des produits de dons, legs et subventions ; - des produits de l'aliénation des biens de la collectivité." This is a direct structural analogue to the régions' Article 80 in Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation) — the same enumeration pattern/order, evidencing a consistent national budget-composition template across both régional and Djibouti-Ville tiers. Also confirmed on the same page: the budget must be voted "avant le 1er janvier" of the fiscal year, accounts reported by July 1, and deficits exceeding 5% of operating revenue trigger court intervention; Article 52 gives the Council authority to set local taxes within legal limits.

reports.title: Loi n°107/AN/00/4ème L du 29 octobre 2000 relative aux lois des Finances
reports.description: Djibouti's organic public-finance/budget law, as described on the Ministère du Budget's own site (budget.gouv.dj). Verbatim quote on scope: "Elle s'applique à l'État, aux collectivités régionales et aux établissements publiques" [sic, "établissements publiques" as printed on the source page] — establishing that this organic law's public-accounting rules apply to régional collectivités as well as the État, the general statutory framework that the Plans de Développement Régional (see dj-pdr-* series) and Loi 174's Article 80/93 budget provisions sit underneath. Article 1, verbatim: "fixe les règles fondamentales relatives à la nature, au contenu, à la procédure d'élaboration, de présentation et d'adoption des lois de finances." Article 4 identifies three types of finance laws: loi de finances de l'année (initiale), loi de finances rectificative, and loi de règlement.

reports.title: Plan de Développement Régional (PDR) 2021-2025 de la Région de Tadjourah
reports.publisher: Conseil Régional de Tadjourah / Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation, République de Djibouti
reports.description: Government-authored five-year regional development/budget plan for Tadjourah, one of the five régions created by Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation). Financial mobilization table ("Tableau de mobilisation financière"), TOTAL row by year, verbatim as extracted: "118 124 000 (2021) / 159 624 000 (2022) / 180 124 000 (2023) / 100 624 000 (2024) / 100 924 000 (2025) FDJ; GRAND TOTAL 659 420 000 FDJ." By source, verbatim: "Fiscalité (patente, foncier, matériels)" 56 300 000 FDJ; "Fiscalité locale" 3 120 000 FDJ; "Dotation de l'État" 270 000 000 FDJ (roughly 41% of total mobilized resources); "Subvention ADIL" 250 000 000 FDJ; "HYDROPONIE" 80 000 000 FDJ. The "Dotation de l'État" line is a directly quantified, named instantiation of the "dotation globale" state-to-région fiscal-transfer mechanism established by Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 93 (see dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation). Caveat: these figures were extracted via an automated fetch tool's summarization of the source PDF and have not been independently re-verified digit-by-digit against the raw PDF bytes; recommended for a raw-text re-extraction pass in a future round before treating exact figures as fully audited.

reports.title: Plan de Développement Régional (PDR) 2021-2025 de la Région d'Ali-Sabieh
reports.publisher: Conseil Régional Ali-Sabieh / Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation, République de Djibouti
reports.description: Government-authored five-year regional development/budget plan for Ali-Sabieh, one of the five régions created by Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation). Cover page, verbatim: "CONSEIL REGIONAL ALI-SABIEH." Section VI action matrix, tourism-sector line item, verbatim: "Construire un hôtel touristique équipé avec des chambres d'hébergement, une cuisine, un restaurant, un hall d'accueil et de rafraîchissement au Grand Barra" — budgeted at 35 000 000 FDJ. No single aggregate five-year budget total was located for Ali-Sabieh (unlike the Tadjourah and Obock PDRs); costs are itemized per action only in the material reviewed this round.

reports.title: Plan de Développement Régional (PDR) 2021-2025 de la Région de Dikhil
reports.publisher: Conseil Régional de Dikhil / Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation, République de Djibouti
reports.description: Government-authored five-year regional development/budget plan for Dikhil, one of the five régions created by Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation). Investment-program/action-matrix line items, verbatim: "Extension du réseau distribution d'eau pour le secteur Mandaitou" — 20 000 000 DJF; "Augmention de capacité du réservoir de 100m3 pour le secteur Harou" — 5 000 000 DJF ["Augmention" reproduced as printed in the source document, not a transcription error]. Per fetch-tool summary (not independently re-verified verbatim beyond the two quoted line items above), water/agriculture infrastructure line items across the plan range roughly 2 000 000-30 000 000 DJF.

reports.title: Plan de Développement Régional (PDR) 2021-2025 de la Région d'Obock
reports.publisher: Conseil Régional d'Obock / Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation, République de Djibouti
reports.description: Government-authored five-year regional development/budget plan for Obock, one of the five régions created by Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation). Revenue table, TOTAL by year, verbatim as extracted: "152 505 000 Fdj 169 645 000 Fdj 149 645 000 Fdj 59 645 000 Fdj 59 645 000 Fdj 591 085 000 Fdj" (2021-2025 figures followed by the grand total). Competency-transfer discussion, verbatim: "Le décret n°2007 – 0099 – PR – MID ait transféré 9 domaines de compétences au Conseil Régional" [verb form "ait transféré" reproduced as extracted, possibly a subjunctive/typo in the source document; Décret n°2007-0099-PR-MID itself was not independently located or fetched this round]. Implementation-status admission, verbatim: "à ce jour, seule celle de l'Etat Civil est réellement effective au niveau du Chef-lieu" — a rare, directly quotable primary-government admission that of the nine competencies formally decentralized to régional councils by decree in 2007, only civil-status registration is actually operative, and only at the chef-lieu (regional capital), not in sub-prefectures — a candid, present-tense statement of the gap between Djibouti's decentralization law-on-paper and its practice.

dependencies.basis: Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 4 explicitly anticipates and names Djibouti-Ville's carve-out from the régional system: "...Djibouti-Ville qui fera l'objet d'un statut spécial." Loi n°122/AN/05, enacted three years later, is precisely that special statute — the two laws share the same subject entity (Djibouti-Ville) and a direct sequential textual reference from the earlier law to the later one.

The Tadjourah PDR's financial mobilization table includes a named, quantified "Dotation de l'État" line item (270 000 000 FDJ, ~41% of total mobilized resources) that is the region's own budgeted instantiation of the "dotation globale" state-to-région fiscal-transfer mechanism created by Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 93 ("Une dotation globale sera consentie par État pour assurer le fonctionnement des régions décentralisées").

The Conseil Régional Ali-Sabieh, author/subject of this PDR, is one of the five régional collectivités territoriales explicitly created by name in Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 2 ("...Régions d'Arta, d'Ali Sabieh, de Dikhil, d'Obock et de Tadjourah"); the PDR is a planning/budget product of that legally-created entity.

The Conseil Régional de Dikhil, author/subject of this PDR, is one of the five régional collectivités territoriales explicitly created by name in Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 2; the PDR is a planning/budget product of that legally-created entity.

The Conseil Régional d'Obock, author/subject of this PDR, is one of the five régional collectivités territoriales explicitly created by name in Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 2; the PDR is a planning/budget product of that legally-created entity.

_dropped.why: Loi 107's own text asserts general scope over 'l'État, aux collectivités régionales et aux établissements publiques,' and it is very likely the organic legal framework under which Loi 174 Article 80/93 and the PDR budgets operate — but neither document was found this round to explicitly name or cite the other by number/date. Consistent with this branch's practice of not minting an inferred structural relationship as a live dependency edge absent a direct textual cross-reference (cf. the DR Congo cd-cbmt-2024-2026/cd-constitution-provinces-revenue precedent). Flagged as a lead for a future round with closer full-text comparison of both laws.

RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (lead-chasing follow-up round, dj-leadchase-loi149.json). The full verbatim text (8 pages, Articles 1-24) was obtained via a text-extraction reader-proxy (r.jina.ai) fetching the same government URL, cross-validated against an independent WebFetch AI-summarization pass of the same URL (matched verbatim wherever both quoted the same passage) — clearing this schema's verbatim-quote requirement. Minted dj-loi-149-2011-amendement and wired both documented amendment targets: dj-loi-149-2011-amendement -> dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation (this edge, on Article 1 and Article 4 modifying Loi 174's terminology and Article 7) and dj-loi-149-2011-amendement -> dj-loi-122-2005-ville-statut (a second edge, on Article 2 adding an alinéa to Loi 122's Article 6) — both relationship_type cites. Note: the quoted operative articles (1, 2, 4) actually verbatim-confirmed this round concern council terminology, composition and governance structure, not the finance/budget articles (97, 99, 101) this entry's earlier AI-paraphrased summary had flagged as amended — those article numbers were not independently re-confirmed verbatim this round and remain an open sub-lead if the finance-article amendments specifically matter to a future session. The government's own domain (decentralisation.gouv.dj) still has a broken TLS certificate chain for direct tooling access, confirmed again this round; flagged as an access-method caveat on the new node. Original entry follows.

Loi n°149/AN/11/6ème L (promulgated 8 December 2011) amends both Loi 174/AN/02 (decentralization/régions) and Article 6 of Loi 122/AN/05 (Djibouti-Ville statute) — confirmed exact title, promulgation date, and the list of amended article numbers (7, 16, 17, 20, 36, 37, 40, 41, 42, 48, 54, 64, 65, 67, 71, 97, 98, 99, 101 of Loi 174; Article 98 fully suppressed), including several finance/budget articles (97, 99, 101) directly adjacent to Articles 80/93. However, this content was obtained only as an AI-paraphrased fetch-tool summary, not word-for-word French text, and per this schema's requirement for actual verbatim quotes, is not minted as a report node this round. Successfully fetched from decentralisation.gouv.dj (URL: https://decentralisation.gouv.dj/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/Djibouti-Loi-2011-149-modifiant-174-et-122.pdf) — a real lead for a future round's verbatim-text pass, particularly on the amended finance articles.

A fifth PDR exists for the Région d'Arta (URL: https://decentralisation.gouv.dj/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PDR-Arta-2021-2025.pdf, confirmed reachable), covering nine sectors with individual project budgets reported to range 1 000 000-35 000 000 FDJ. However, the only content obtained this round was an AI-paraphrased, internally ambiguous fetch-tool summary of one tourism line item ('20 million to 15 million FDJ' near Karta-Layta, phrasing order unclear) rather than verbatim French text. Not minted as a report node this round pending a re-fetch for exact quotable text.

The Obock PDR's own text names 'le décret n°2007 – 0099 – PR – MID' as the legal basis transferring nine domaines de compétences to the Conseil Régional. This decree was not independently located or fetched this round and has no corpus node yet. A genuine lead for a future session: if located and verbatim-verified, it would be the direct legal-basis target for the PDR's competency-transfer quote.

_dropped.edge: egouv.dj régions population figures <-> presidence.dj régions population figures
_dropped.why: Two Djiboutian government web sources disagree on 2021 régional population figures for the same nominal reference year: egouv.dj reports Ali-Sabieh ~102,618, Tadjourah ~102,329, Dikhil ~104,977, Obock ~44,678, Arta ~50,017; presidence.dj reports Ali Sabieh 99,916, Dikhil 111,457, Tadjourah 135,149, Obock 55,044, Arta 84,777 (summing to 486,343). Neither figure set was independently verified as the more authoritative one this round, and the presidence.dj figures were themselves only obtained as an AI-summarized paraphrase, not raw verbatim text. Djibouti-Ville's demographic dominance (commonly cited as 60%+ of the national population) could not be independently computed from a single primary source this round, since no primary document was found stating both the national total and Djibouti-Ville's share directly — any such percentage would currently be derived arithmetic, not a quoted primary fact. Recorded as an open discrepancy for a future round rather than picking one source arbitrarily.

Djibouti's March 2023 PEFA public-finance-management assessment ("RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI — ÉVALUATION DE LA PERFORMANCE DU SYSTEME DE GESTION DES FINANCES PUBLIQUES SUIVANT LA METHODOLOGIE PEFA," URL: https://www.pefa.org/sites/pefa/files/2023-07/DJ-Mar23-PFMPR-Public%20with%20PEFA%20Check.pdf) verbatim-confirms the '6 collectivités territoriales = 5 régions + Djibouti-Ville' structure already independently established via Loi 174 Article 2 and Loi 122 ("Les collectivités territoriales au nombre de 6 comprennent 5 régions et la ville de Djibouti composée de trois communes"), but per its own framing was prepared 'at the request of the Government of Djibouti and financed by the World Bank, European Union and French Development Agency' with PEFA Secretariat quality assurance — mixed authorship, not a clean primary-government document per this branch's evidence rule. Used as corroboration only, not minted as its own report node.

Checked the Cour des Comptes de Djibouti's own most recent annual public report (Rapport Général Annuel Public 2022/2023, Tome 1, adopted 29 December 2024, hosted on the Cour's own domain courdescomptesdjibouti.com) and, separately, its 2021 edition (hosted on AISCCUF's site, a Francophone supreme-audit-institutions association mirroring the Cour's own report) — neither contains any chapter, section, or audit finding disaggregated by named région or by Djibouti-Ville/collectivités territoriales; both are national-level budget-execution, central-administration, DGI, and public-enterprise audits only. Checked across two separate report years/editions, confirming this is a genuine institutional-coverage gap rather than a one-off access failure.

villededjibouti.dj was confirmed as the genuine official site of Djibouti-Ville's municipal government (meta author tag and branding confirm official status), but its homepage contains no budget documents, financial reports, or expenditure data, and no distinct finance/budget subpage was located this round — the site is oriented toward citizen e-services (permits, civil-status requests) rather than fiscal transparency.

_dropped.edge: igad fiscal-transfer or CPI-harmonization framework for Djibouti
_dropped.why: Unlike COMESA (already cited in dj-snds-2011-2015 for trade-statistics harmonization) or SADC/EAC (which have documented Harmonised CPI frameworks), no IGAD document was found establishing a regional statistical-harmonization framework or a fiscal-transfer/member-contribution formula specific to Djibouti. IGAD's own public materials (igad.int) center on peace/security, migration, plastic-pollution, and refugee-education topics. A genuine searched-for absence, not a technical access failure.
